children.name: pinneapple_hub.experiment_card
children.doc:
A model card generated from an experiment record, validated in the same call (#40).

The hub already refuses a card whose ``validation_metrics`` are empty. What it could not do is *produce* one: the
numbers were typed in by hand from a run somebody remembered. This builds the card from the record the run wrote —
``experiment.json`` and ``result.json`` — so the metrics are the recorded ones, the cost is the measured wall time,
and the validity domain is the box the problem was solved in.

    >>> from pinneapple_hub.experiment_card import card_from_record, generate_and_validate
    >>> card = card_from_record("runs/burgers_pinn")        # doctest: +SKIP
    >>> card.validate(require_cost=True, require_validity=True)   # doctest: +SKIP
    []

What it will not do: fill a field it does not have. A record with no reference solution gets no
``validation_metrics`` (the card is refused for the right reason), and a run with no measured time gets no cost.

classes.doc: A card and the verdict on it: what was generated, and every reason it would be refused.

functions.sig: (directory: str | Path, *, name: str = '', license: str = 'apache-2.0', citation: str = '', description: str = '', task: str = '', extra_limitations: list[str] | None = None, model: Any = None) -> ModelCard
functions.doc:
Build the card from a record written by ``Experiment.save`` + ``ExperimentResult.save``.

Raises ``FileNotFoundError`` when the record is not there and ``ValueError`` when it has no metrics: a card
without a computed number is what the hub refuses, so building one would only move the refusal downstream.

functions.doc: The one command: build the card and run the hub's own validation, including cost and validity.

functions.name: cli
functions.doc:
``pinneapple model-card <record>``: generate the card, validate it, and write it.

Exit codes: ``0`` the card passed, ``1`` it was generated and refused (the reasons are printed), ``2`` no record
or a bad invocation. A refused card is written anyway when ``--out`` is given — the reasons are the useful part,
and throwing the draft away would hide which field the record could not fill.

children.name: pinneapple_hub.hub
children.doc:
``push_to_hub`` / ``from_pretrained`` for PINNeAPPle models, built on the
Hugging Face Hub's own storage/auth/versioning infrastructure rather than
a new hosting service this repository would have to build, operate, and
secure itself. This is a deliberate, common pattern (many domain-specific
libraries piggyback on HF Hub this way) -- the value PINNeAPPle adds is
the ``pinneapple_config.json`` sidecar convention that lets a checkpoint
be reconstructed into a live model without the downloader having to
already know its exact architecture kwargs, plus the ``ModelCard`` (see
``model_card.py``) reproducibility contract every push carries.

Requires the ``hub`` extra (``pip install "pinneapple[hub]"``, i.e.
``huggingface_hub``) and a Hugging Face account/token for anything beyond
downloading public repos.

functions.name: push_to_hub
functions.sig: (model, repo_id: str, model_card: ModelCard, *, architecture: Optional[str] = None, architecture_config: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None, private: bool = False, token: Optional[str] = None, commit_message: str = 'Push model via pinneapple_hub') -> str
functions.doc:
Upload a trained model's weights + architecture config + model card
to a Hugging Face Hub model repo.

Parameters
----------
model : the trained ``nn.Module`` (its ``state_dict()`` is uploaded).
repo_id : ``"username/repo-name"``.
model_card : a :class:`ModelCard` -- ``model_card.validate()`` is run
    first and a non-empty problem list raises (a hub push with no
    checkable validation claim is refused by default; see
    ``ModelCard.validate``'s docstring for why).
architecture, architecture_config : the
    ``pinneapple_neural.architectures.ModelRegistry`` name and the
    kwargs ``ModelRegistry.build(architecture, **architecture_config)``
    needs to reconstruct this exact model shape before loading the
    state_dict back in :func:`from_pretrained`. Defaults to
    ``model_card.architecture``/``model_card.architecture_config`` if
    not given explicitly.
private : create the repo as private if it doesn't exist yet.
token : HF token; falls back to the ``huggingface_hub`` CLI's cached
    login (``huggingface-cli login``) if not given.

Returns
-------
The repo URL.

functions.sig: (repo_id: str, *, revision: str = 'main', device: str = 'cpu', token: Optional[str] = None)
functions.doc:
Download and reconstruct a model pushed with :func:`push_to_hub`.

children.name: pinneapple_hub.library.compose
children.doc:
"Create your own": a custom tool composed from existing blocks (Flow Studio node types, optionally a bundled flow
to start from and a library geometry), returned as a flow document and the Python that runs it.

    from pinneapple_hub.library.compose import compose
    out = compose({"name": "Heat rod", "blocks": [
        {"type": "geometry.domain", "params": {"dimension": 1}},
        {"type": "geometry.mesh", "params": {"n": 41}}]})
    out["flow"]          # pinneapple-flow/1 document (open it in Flow Studio, or pf.run it)
    out["code"]          # Python: build the flow, validate, run, print each node's metrics
    out["issues"]        # validation issues (pinneapple_flow.validate_flow) and inputs that could not be wired

A whole flow can be the start too (``"flow": <pinneapple-flow/1 document>``, what Flow Studio's "Publish to Hub"
sends), and ``"expose": [{"node": id, "param": name}]`` turns those parameters into variables at the top of the
generated Python, so the published tool reads as a function of them.

Blocks are appended in order; each new block's required inputs are wired from the block before it, then from that
block's ancestors, then from any earlier block with a compatible output
(:func:`pinneapple_flow.lab_status.insert_nodes`). Only registered node types are accepted, and parameters are
checked against each node's schema, so a composed tool never contains code a visitor typed.

generated library calls), by palette section, with its ports and parameters.

children.name: pinneapple_hub.library.flowlink
children.doc:
The Hub and Flow Studio on one registry: a ready flow around any node type, and links between the two apps.

    from pinneapple_hub.library.flowlink import flow_for_node, flow_link, add_link
    out = flow_for_node("geometry.mesh", {"n": 41})     # {"flow", "issues", "ok", "source", "node"}
    flow_link(out["flow"], base="http://127.0.0.1:8765")   # Flow Studio opens it (?flow=<base64url JSON>)
    add_link("geometry.mesh", {"n": 41}, base=...)          # Flow Studio adds the node to a flow the user picks (?add=)

``flow_for_node`` builds *inputs -> the tool -> a report*:

1. when a bundled flow (``pinneapple_flow/flows``) uses the node type, its upstream nodes with their wiring and
   parameters, as committed and validated there;
2. otherwise a producer for each required input, chosen among node types without required inputs of their own (or,
   up to three levels, with inputs that can be produced the same way) whose output feeds that input type;
3. then ``export.report`` on the node's outputs (``items: any``), unless the node already ends in a report.

Every node is a registered type and every parameter is checked against its schema (``NodeSpec.check_params``); the
wiring is ``pinneapple_flow.lab_status.insert_nodes``, the one the Flow Studio GUI uses.

children.name: pinneapple_hub.library.flowruns
children.doc:
Recorded runs of the bundled flows (``pinneapple_flow/flows``), shown in the Hub on each flow's page and on the
page of every node type the flow uses.

    python -m pinneapple_hub.library flowruns [names ...]    # run them headless, write data/web/hub/flow_runs.json
    from pinneapple_hub.library.flowruns import read_flow_runs, runs_for_node
    runs_for_node(read_flow_runs(), "geometry.mesh")          # [{flow, node, status, metrics, summary}, ...]

Each flow runs in the sandbox (:func:`pinneapple_hub.library.sandbox.run_snippet`, its own interpreter and time limit)
with ``pinneapple_flow.run``; what is kept per node is its status and the metrics and summary its report holds. A run
is current while the flow file has the SHA-256 it was recorded with; a flow that fails or times out is recorded as
such, with the error, and its nodes show nothing.

children.name: pinneapple_hub.library.sandbox
children.doc:
Run a code snippet in a short-lived, separate interpreter and keep what it printed and drew.

    from pinneapple_hub.library.sandbox import run_snippet
    r = run_snippet('import pinneapple as pp\nprint(pp.geometries.list()[:3])', timeout=60)
    r["ok"], r["stdout"], r["seconds"], r["figures"]       # figures: PNG bytes of the matplotlib figures left open

The snippet runs in a fresh temporary directory (its working directory, deleted afterwards) with matplotlib on
Agg, no GPU, a wall-clock time limit and, on POSIX, address-space / CPU-time / file-size limits (``setrlimit``) so a
runaway snippet is killed with every process it started. Network access is not blocked here: deploy the app that
calls this on a network without egress (apps/deploy) when the snippets come from visitors.

children.name: pinneapple_hub.library.sources
children.doc:
Where the Hub's items come from. Each collector reads one existing source of the repository and returns items in
the Hub format (see :mod:`pinneapple_hub.library`); nothing here is written by hand.

=================  =================================================================================================
``models``         the zoo manifest and the bundled model cards (``pinneapple_hub/zoo``), an example row of each
                   model's own held-out test split, the browser ONNX graphs (``data/web/zoo``)
``datasets``       the zoo manifest's datasets (``pp.datasets``)
``geometries``     the geometry library (``pinneapple_design.geometry_library``: ``web.index()`` and the manifest)
``flows``          the bundled flows of Flow Studio (``pinneapple_flow/flows``)
``nodes``          the curated node types of Flow Studio's palette (``pinneapple_flow.REGISTRY``)
``recipes``        the Python blocks of AGENTS.md and the examples of the module reference
                   (``scripts/reference/content.py``, recorded by ``scripts/reference/run_examples.py``)
``apis``           the "Use these APIs first" table of AGENTS.md, resolved to the public functions it names
``agent_tools``    the tools of the MCP server (``pinneapple_mcp.server``)
``examples``       the experiments page of the Lab (``pinneapple_lab.explorer.collect``): every ``examples/*``
                   manifest and every Lab item, with its A-F seal and six-stage trust card
=================  =================================================================================================

children.doc:
The PINNeAPPle Hub index: every ready-made thing in the repository -- tools (public functions, Flow Studio nodes,
recipes, MCP tools), trained models, geometries, datasets, flows and examples -- as one generated list, each item
with a runnable snippet whose recorded run is checked by a test.

    from pinneapple_hub import library as hub
    index = hub.load_index()                              # data/web/hub/index.json (generated, not committed)
    hits = hub.search(index, "airfoil", kind="model")     # ranked items
    item = hub.get(index, "geometry:f1_car")
    item["code"], item["run"]["stdout"], item["files"], item["links"]["guide"]

    python -m pinneapple_hub.library build              # regenerate index.json from the sources
    python -m pinneapple_hub.library run [--stale]      # run every snippet, record its output (snippet_runs/)
    python -m pinneapple_hub.library check              # index is current, every run ok, files and links exist

An item: ``id`` (``<kind-prefix>:<name>``), ``kind`` (tool, model, geometry, dataset, flow, example; tools have a
``subkind`` and one of 20 task ``category`` slugs, :mod:`.categories`), ``title``, ``summary``, ``description``,
``domain`` (``pinneapple_lab.manifest.domain_of``), ``tags``,
``quality`` (a Lab A-F seal with its six-stage trust card, a zoo decision, or None), ``code`` (the snippet),
``run`` (its recorded run: ok, stdout, seconds, figures), ``results`` (measured numbers and figures of the source),
``examples`` (ids of related items), ``files`` (repo paths and download URLs), ``links`` (guide, reference, source,
Flow Studio). Where each kind comes from: :mod:`.sources`. "Create your own": :mod:`.compose`. Saved items:
:mod:`.myhub`. Snippet runner: :mod:`.sandbox`.

``index.json`` is derived and git-ignored: :func:`load_index` builds and caches it on first use, the Hub image
builds it at ``docker build``. The recorded runs it attaches are committed, one file per item under
``snippet_runs/``, so two pull requests that record different snippets never touch the same file.

children.name: pinneapple_hub.model_card
children.doc:
``ModelCard``: the reproducibility contract every hub-pushed model
carries.

Why this exists: a physical claim ("matches DNS to 2%") is only as good
as its provenance. Without architecture + exact training config + data
lineage + a computed (not just asserted) validation-metrics block bound to
the weights, a downloaded checkpoint's claims cannot be re-checked by
anyone but the person who trained it -- exactly the kind of unverifiable
claim ``pinneapple_llm``'s ``PhysicsGuardrail`` (see that module) exists to
catch. ``ModelCard`` is the structured version of what this very project's
own ``problem_config.json`` recorded by hand (physics/domain/BC/IC/
forcing/data/training/reference sections) for a single case; this is the
general, hub-wide schema.

methods.doc: Store the latest TrustReport (a ``TrustReport`` or its ``to_dict()``); a new report clears an old override.

methods.doc: Allow publication despite a REJECT; the reason is recorded in the card.

methods.sig: (*, require_cost: bool = False, require_validity: bool = False) -> List[str]
methods.doc:
Return a list of schema problems (empty = passes). Does not

children.name: pinneapple_hub.verified_card
children.doc:
Model cards whose ``validation_metrics`` come only from a guardrail run against the model, refused otherwise.

:func:`certify_model` builds (or loads) a model for a registered preset, trains it when no weights are given,
runs :class:`pinneapple_llm.PhysicsGuardrail` on it and builds a :class:`~pinneapple_hub.model_card.ModelCard`
with :func:`card_from_guardrail`: every numeric check value goes into ``validation_metrics`` under the check's
name, every pass/fail-only check as ``<name>_passed`` (1.0 / 0.0), and ``reference_source`` says what was run on
how many fresh points. A card that fails ``ModelCard.validate()`` (for example because nothing computable ran)
raises :class:`CardRefused` instead of being returned, the same rule ``push_to_hub`` applies.

Re-auditing an existing card can only re-run the schema check: the weights and the exact preset kwargs behind a
card's numbers do not travel in the card JSON, so its physics claims cannot be re-executed from it alone.

Moved here from the PINNeAPPle-apps ``physics_verified_model_cards`` product (GovernedCard); the HTTP service is
``apps/governed_card``.

classes.name: CardRefused
classes.doc: The card built from a guardrail run did not pass ``ModelCard.validate()``; ``.problems`` lists why.

``pp.zoo.anchors``: the published model family, grouped by the engineering problem it answers.

The zoo is a catalogue of everything that passed the gate; an *anchor* is the opposite view -- one named,
productised entry per problem, pointing at the model(s) that answer it, and carrying the numbers that already
exist in their model cards. Nothing here invents a metric: every value is read from ``manifest.json`` and the
model card, so the family page cannot drift from what ships (``tests/test_zoo_anchors.py`` checks it).

    data = pp.zoo.anchors.public()                 # JSON for the site's /modelos page

not a product: :func:`problems` lists those, and the test fails on a non-empty list.

children.name: pinneapple_hub.zoo.checks
children.doc:
Per-query trust checks of the zoo models, and the verdict they add up to.

``pp.zoo.validate`` judges a model as a whole (its metrics, its physics checks). This module judges one *query*:
is this input inside the validity range, are the outputs physical, does the ensemble agree as well as it did on
held-out data, do the model's physics checks hold *here*? Each check has the rule ID of ``pinneapple check``
(PC601 out-of-range query, PC602 sparse region, PC402/PC403 unphysical or non-finite output, PC302 model residual).

A check is a value computed from the query and a comparison with a limit (``check_spec``). The values come from a
``torch`` module (:func:`checks_module`), the same one :func:`pinneapple_hub.zoo.export.export_onnx` puts in the
ONNX graph, so a browser evaluating the graph and Python evaluating :func:`query_checks` agree to float precision.
:func:`verdict` turns the statuses into one decision: any failing check -> ``fail`` ("outside the validity range,
an extrapolation"), any warning -> ``warn`` ("use with caution"), else ``pass``. Design constraints (``kind ==
"design"``) are reported but never enter the verdict: they say whether a design is acceptable, not whether the model
can be trusted.

    import pinneapple as pp
    r = pp.zoo.query_checks("airfoil_cst_rans_mlp", {"T0": .17, "T1": .15, "T2": .13, "M0": .02, "M1": .07,
                                                     "M2": .06, "alpha_deg": 16})[0]
    r["verdict"]["status"]       # 'fail': alpha 16 is beyond the trained range

functions.doc: Whether the model has per-query checks (:func:`query_checks`); otherwise only ``in_range`` applies.

functions.name: check_spec
functions.doc:
The declarative description of a model's query checks: ``checks`` (one entry per column of the ``checks``
output: id, rule, name, op, limit, severity, kind, group, detail template), ``aux`` (names of the ``aux``
columns the templates use), ``groups`` (display name and rule of grouped checks) and ``verdicts``.

functions.doc: ``torch.nn.Module``: query rows (m, d) -> (values (m, C), aux (m, A)) of :func:`check_spec`.

functions.name: check_values
functions.doc: (values, aux) of the query checks for rows ``X`` (physical inputs, card order).

functions.name: compare
functions.doc: ``value op limit``; NaN never passes.

functions.name: evaluate
functions.sig: (spec: Mapping[str, Any], values: Sequence[float], aux: Sequence[float]) -> dict[str, Any]
functions.doc:
Statuses, details and the verdict for one row of check values (the browser does the same with the graph's
outputs).

functions.doc: The worst status of the trust checks (design constraints excluded) with its title and explanation.

functions.sig: (model: str | ZooModel, inputs, *, offline: bool | None = None) -> list[dict[str, Any]]
functions.doc:
The query checks and the verdict for each input row (a mapping of named columns or an (n, d) array).

Returns one ``{"checks": [...], "verdict": {"status", "title", "text"}}`` per row; each check carries its
``status`` (pass / warn / fail), ``value``, ``limit``, rule ID and a filled-in ``detail_text``.

children.doc:
``pp.datasets``: ready-made, verified datasets in one line.

    import pinneapple as pp
    pp.datasets.list()                                   # names
    pp.datasets.info("airfoil_rans_cst_re4e6")           # schema, splits, provenance, verification, licence
    test = pp.datasets.load("airfoil_rans_cst_re4e6", split="test")

holding every split, or one ``<split>.npz`` per split (large datasets; a split may be sharded into ``<split>-NN.npz``,
concatenated along the rows on load, and only the requested split is downloaded). Small files are bundled with the
package; the others are downloaded once from the Hugging Face Hub (``PINNeAPPle-Labs/<name>``), checked against the
SHA-256 in the manifest and cached (see ``pinneapple_hub.zoo._artifacts``).

children.name: pinneapple_hub.zoo.demo
children.doc:
What the zoo's demo Space shows, computed by the library: each model's prediction along a sweep of each input,
with its ensemble spread or conformal bound and where its query checks warn or fail, and the files of the static
Space that shows them.

The Space (``huggingface.co/spaces/PINNeAPPle-Labs/zoo-demo``, a static Space: no server) is the page in
``apps/zoo_space/`` over the files :func:`export_space` writes:

* ``models/<name>.sweeps.json`` (:func:`precompute`): for every input, a sweep from 15 % below to 15 % above its
  range, the other inputs at a held-out test case; the predictions, their band, and the verdict of the query checks
  at every point (pass / warn / fail); the checks at the test case and the model's trust decision;
* ``models/<name>.onnx`` and ``models/<name>.json`` (:func:`pinneapple_hub.zoo.web.export_web`): the model and its
  query checks as one ONNX graph, so the page can evaluate the visitor's own inputs in the browser;
* ``lib/onnx.js``, ``lib/zoo.js``: the browser runtime (a dependency-free ONNX interpreter and the JS twin of
  :func:`pinneapple_hub.zoo.checks.evaluate`; ``tests/js/zoo_space.test.mjs`` checks it against these files).

The same calls work in a notebook:

    from pinneapple_hub.zoo import demo
    c = demo.controls("airfoil_cst_rans_mlp")                      # inputs, units, ranges, a held-out case
    r = demo.sweep("airfoil_cst_rans_mlp", {k["name"]: k["value"] for k in c}, vary="alpha_deg")
    r["status"]                                                     # pass / warn / fail along the sweep

children.name: pinneapple_hub.zoo.export
children.doc:
ONNX export of zoo models and their per-query trust checks.

``export_onnx(name, path)`` writes one ONNX graph from the model card's physical inputs to its physical outputs:
pre-processing (CST encoding, log features, normalisation) and post-processing (denormalisation, exp, ensemble mean
and spread, conformal bound) are inside the graph, so any ONNX runtime gives the same numbers as ``predict``.
With ``checks=True`` the graph takes a second input, ``query``, and also returns the values of the model's query
checks (:mod:`pinneapple_hub.zoo.checks`) for those rows. :func:`onnx_parity` measures the largest difference
between a graph and the PyTorch model on the zoo's held-out and independent-reference inputs.

functions.name: predictor_module
functions.doc: ``torch.nn.Module`` mapping the card's inputs (n, d) to a tuple of outputs (see :func:`output_names`).

functions.name: output_names
functions.doc: ONNX output -> the ``predict`` keys of its columns.

functions.name: as_graph_outputs
functions.sig: (zm: ZooModel, pred: dict[str, np.ndarray]) -> dict[str, np.ndarray]
functions.doc: ``predict`` output laid out like the graph's outputs.

functions.name: output_scale
functions.doc:
Per column, the scale of the parity tolerance: NaN = relative to the value (positive, log-modelled outputs:
Cd, R, dP; L/D relative to max(|L/D|, y_std(Cl) / Cd), the error a Cl within tolerance implies), otherwise the
network's standardisation scale.

functions.name: parity_error
functions.sig: (zm: ZooModel, ref: dict[str, np.ndarray], got: dict[str, np.ndarray]) -> float
functions.doc:
Largest |got - ref| / scale over every output column (see :func:`output_scale`). Spreads (``std``, ``LD_std``)
are measured relative to the quantity they spread around.

functions.name: export_bytes
functions.doc: The ONNX graph of a loaded zoo model (see :func:`export_onnx`).

functions.name: export_onnx
functions.sig: (name: str | ZooModel, path: str | Path, *, checks: bool = False, check_parity: bool = True, offline: bool | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]
functions.doc:
Export a zoo model to ONNX at ``path``. The graph maps the card's inputs (input ``x``, shape (n, d)) to its
outputs; with ``checks=True`` it also takes ``query`` (m, d) and returns the query-check values (``checks``,
``aux``; see :func:`pinneapple_hub.zoo.checks.check_spec`). Unless ``check_parity=False`` the export is refused
(``ValueError``) when the predictions differ from the PyTorch model by more than 1e-5 (:func:`onnx_parity`) or a
query-check status differs from Python away from its limit (:func:`checks_parity`).
Returns ``{"path", "bytes", "sha256", "parity", "inputs", "outputs"}``.

functions.name: parity_inputs
functions.sig: (zm: ZooModel, *, n_random: int = 500, seed: int = 7) -> np.ndarray
functions.doc:
The model's held-out and independent-reference inputs (every evaluation split) plus random points inside the
validity box (when the box describes every input).

functions.sig: (data: bytes | str | Path, X: np.ndarray, query: np.ndarray | None = None) -> dict[str, np.ndarray]
functions.doc: Run a graph in onnxruntime (CPU, one thread) and return its outputs by name (float64).

functions.name: onnx_parity
functions.sig: (name: str | ZooModel, onnx_model: bytes | str | Path, X: np.ndarray | None = None, *, offline: bool | None = None) -> float
functions.doc:
Largest scaled difference (:func:`parity_error`) between an exported graph's predictions and
``ZooModel.predict`` on ``X`` (default :func:`parity_inputs`).

functions.name: checks_parity
functions.sig: (name: str | ZooModel, onnx_model: bytes | str | Path, X: np.ndarray | None = None, *, offline: bool | None = None) -> dict[str, float]
functions.doc:
Compare the query checks of a graph exported with ``checks=True`` with
:func:`pinneapple_hub.zoo.checks.check_values`: the largest value difference (relative to max(|value|, 1)) and
the number of rows where a status differs although the value is farther than ``CHECK_TOL`` from its limit
(float32 finite differences can flip a status only right at a limit).

children.name: pinneapple_hub.zoo.parquet
children.doc:
Parquet copies of the zoo datasets, for the Hugging Face dataset viewer and ``datasets.load_dataset``.

The npz files stay the source of truth: their SHA-256 are in the manifest and ``pp.datasets.load`` reads them. The
Parquet files are derived from them, deterministically (same npz and same pyarrow version -> same bytes):

* each split becomes ``data/<config>/<split>-NNNNN.parquet``. Splits with the same columns share a config; the
  config holding ``train`` (else ``test``, else the first split) is ``default``, any other one is named after its
  first split (a grid, a convergence study, an independent reference with other columns);
* scalar columns stay plain columns; an array column becomes a fixed-size list column of the same shape (``List(
  List(float32, length=64), length=64)`` in ``datasets``; ``with_format("numpy")`` gives the arrays back);
* a sample larger than :data:`EXPLODE_ROW_BYTES` whose array columns share a leading axis (a time series of fields)
  is stored as one row per step of that axis, with ``sample`` (row of the npz split) and ``step`` columns; the
  per-sample columns are repeated on every step. This keeps every row small enough for the viewer;
* a shard holds at most :data:`MAX_SHARD_BYTES` of uncompressed data and a row group at most :data:`ROW_GROUP_BYTES`,
  so the viewer can page any split;
* each field's metadata keeps its numpy dtype and per-row shape, so :func:`read_parquet` returns the npz arrays bit
  for bit.

    from pinneapple_hub.zoo import parquet
    layout = parquet.write_dataset("darcy_2d_li2021", parquet.read_npz(paths), "out/")   # files + features
    parquet.read_parquet(layout["configs"][0]["splits"][0]["paths"])                     # {column: array}

children.name: pinneapple_hub.zoo.publish
children.doc:
Publish the zoo to the Hugging Face Hub and check what the Hub serves (``scripts/zoo/publish_to_hub.py`` is the
command line, ``.github/workflows/publish-zoo.yml`` runs it).

One repo per item under ``PINNeAPPle-Labs`` (model repos for models, dataset repos for datasets), tagged with the
item's ``revision``, plus one Space for the demo:

* **datasets**: the npz files of the manifest (the library's format, SHA-256 checked), the Parquet files derived from
  them (:mod:`pinneapple_hub.zoo.parquet`, what the dataset viewer and ``datasets.load_dataset`` read) and the card
  (:func:`pinneapple_hub.zoo.hub_cards.dataset_card`). A Hub-only dataset (npz too large to bundle) is converted from
  its staged files or, with ``hub_fallback``, from the copy already on the Hub (SHA-256 checked again);
* **models**: ``weights.pt``, ``config.json``, ``model_card.json`` of the manifest plus ``model.safetensors``,
  ``model.onnx`` and ``example.json`` derived from them, and the card (:func:`pinneapple_hub.zoo.hub_cards.model_card`);
* **the Space** ``PINNeAPPle-Labs/zoo-demo``: a static Space (no server) built by :func:`build_space`: the page of
  ``apps/zoo_space`` over the sweeps, bands and check verdicts :mod:`pinneapple_hub.zoo.demo` computes from the
  published models, and the models' ONNX graphs with their query checks for the visitor's own inputs.

Checks after an upload, all anonymous: :func:`verify_files` (every manifest file at the tag, SHA-256),
:func:`verify_viewer` (datasets-server ``is-valid``, ``splits`` and ``first-rows`` of every split),
:func:`verify_models` (load from the Hub, card metrics reproduced, the card's example reproduced by the PyTorch,
safetensors and ONNX copies, the card's "How to use" code run) and :func:`verify_space` (the Space runs and serves its
page and data).

functions.doc:
Upload every item (one commit each) and tag it with its revision; returns the items that failed (each failure

time, and its downloads deleted afterwards (the npz are already on the Hub, so only the Parquet files and the
card are committed).

functions.sig: (out: Path, app_dir: Path, playground_dir: Path, models: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> list[str]
functions.doc:

functions.sig: (token: str, app_dir: Path, playground_dir: Path, *, work: Path | None = None, from_hub: bool = True) -> list[str]

Build the static demo Space (:func:`build_space`) and upload it in one commit, deleting the files of an earlier

functions.name: verify_files
functions.doc:
Download every manifest file anonymously from the item's revision (or the version tag it republishes) and
compare its SHA-256 with the manifest; returns the number of failures. With ``allow_unpublished``, a Hub-only
item that is not on the Hub yet (HTTP 404) is reported but not counted; a wrong checksum always fails.

functions.name: viewer_status
functions.sig: (repo: str, *, timeout: float = 2400, interval: float = 30, get = _get_json, sleep = time.sleep) -> dict[str, Any]
functions.doc:
The dataset viewer's state of one dataset repo: ``is-valid`` (polled until ``preview`` and ``viewer`` are
true or ``timeout``), the configs and splits it found and, per split, the ``first-rows`` answer (rows,
truncated cells, error).

functions.name: verify_viewer
functions.sig: (names: Sequence[str] | None = None, *, timeout: float = 2400, interval: float = 30, get = _get_json, sleep = time.sleep) -> int
functions.doc:
Check the dataset viewer of every dataset (anonymous datasets-server API): ``is-valid`` must say preview and
viewer, every split of the manifest must be listed, and ``first-rows`` of every split must return rows. Prints
one block per dataset; returns the number of datasets that fail.

functions.name: verify_model
functions.doc:
Problems found with the published model ``name`` (empty when none): it is loaded from the Hub with the zoo's
loader (bundled copy ignored, fresh cache); its card metrics must be reproduced on the stored reference
(``pp.zoo.evaluate``); the card's example must be reproduced by the PyTorch weights, by ``model.safetensors``
and by ``model.onnx`` downloaded from the repo; the README's front matter must say what the card promises and
its "How to use" code must run and print the example's outputs.

functions.name: verify_models
functions.doc:
:func:`verify_model` for every model, anonymously (no token), with the bundled copies ignored and an empty
cache; returns the number of models with problems.

functions.name: verify_space
functions.sig: (*, timeout: float = 2400, interval: float = 30, runtime = None, fetch = _fetch, sleep = time.sleep) -> int
functions.doc:
Wait for the demo Space to run and serve its page; 0 when the stage is RUNNING and the page, ``index.json``
and every model's sweeps load (anonymously), 1 otherwise. Prints the stage, hardware and what was fetched.

children.name: pinneapple_hub.zoo.relations
children.doc:
Metamorphic relations the physics of each zoo model implies (#698), checked without any reference solution by
:func:`check_zoo_relations` (``pinneapple_analysis.validation.metamorphic``).

Each model has groups of relations; each group samples its own box of inputs (a nominal design with some inputs
varied), so the relation is tested inside the model's validity range.

* ``airfoil_cst_rans_mlp``: mirroring the camber line and the angle of attack (``M -> -M``, ``alpha -> -alpha``) flips
  the sign of lift and moment and keeps the drag (geometric symmetry of the incompressible flow); lift grows with the
  angle of attack in the attached range (up to 8 degrees, below the stall of the training set).
* ``heatsink_forced_mlp``: more air speed gives no higher thermal resistance and no lower pressure drop; a better
  conductor gives no higher resistance; above 2 m/s the resistance does not depend on the dissipated power (to 2 %).
  Below 2 m/s it does, in the physics engine too (+6.5 % when the power doubles at 0.6 m/s), so it is not tested there.

functions.sig: (model, name: str | None = None, *, n: int = 64, seed: int = 0, search: str = 'random', relations: list[dict[str, Any]] | None = None) -> MetamorphicReport
functions.doc: Run the relations of a zoo model (``model``: a loaded zoo model or anything with the same ``predict``).

children.name: pinneapple_hub.zoo.validation_reports
children.doc:
Stored validation reports of the zoo models (#706): one ``pp.validate`` report per model, kept with the package,
shown in the model's Hub card, and compared with a fresh report before a release.

``build(name)`` writes ``validation_reports/<name>.json``; ``stored(name)`` reads it; ``check_release(name)`` validates
the model as it is now and diffs the result against the stored report: a check that passed and no longer passes is
a regression and blocks the release (``scripts/zoo/validation_reports.py check``, run by the zoo publishing
workflow before any upload).

functions.doc: Validate the zoo model ``name`` and store its report.

functions.name: check_release
functions.doc:
``(diff, fresh report)`` of the model as it is now (or ``model``, e.g. a new version) against its stored
report; ``diff.regressed`` blocks the release. Without a stored report the diff is against an empty one.

children.name: pinneapple_hub.zoo.web
children.doc:
Zoo models for the browser: ONNX graphs with their query checks, model cards and the JS runtime.

    python -m pinneapple_hub.zoo.web data/web/zoo        # what the Playground (apps/playground) serves

:func:`export_web` writes, per model, ``<name>.onnx`` (predictions for ``x`` and the query checks for ``query``,
:func:`pinneapple_hub.zoo.export.export_onnx` with ``checks=True``) and ``<name>.json`` (the model card, the
declarative check spec of :mod:`pinneapple_hub.zoo.checks`, the graph's layout and reference data to plot next to
the predictions). :func:`export_bundle` adds the CST airfoil geometry graphs
(:mod:`pinneapple_design.aero.geometry_onnx`) and ``fixtures.json`` (Python answers for fixed inputs, used by the
JS tests and the Playground's browser test).

The JS runtime that reads these files ships next to this module: ``onnx.js`` (a dependency-free ONNX interpreter)
and ``zoo.js`` (``loadModel``, ``loadAirfoilGeometry``, ``evaluate``: the JS twin of
:func:`pinneapple_hub.zoo.checks.evaluate`). :func:`runtime_dir` returns its folder.

functions.doc:
Reference points to plot next to the predictions: for the airfoil, the held-out OpenFOAM runs and the XFOIL
polar of each NACA preset; for the rover, the held-out Wong-Reece states.

children.doc:
``pp.zoo``: pre-trained, verified PINNeAPPle models in one line -- load, predict, evaluate against the stored
reference, validate (physics checks + validity range), benchmark and fine-tune with a held-out guard.

    import pinneapple as pp
    pp.zoo.list()                                       # ['airfoil_cst_rans_mlp', 'heatsink_forced_mlp', ...]
    card = pp.zoo.info("airfoil_cst_rans_mlp")          # ModelCard: task, inputs/outputs + units, validity range,
                                                        # metrics vs reference, training data, licence, citation
    m = pp.zoo.load("airfoil_cst_rans_mlp")
    m.predict(T0=0.17, T1=0.15, T2=0.13, M0=0.02, M1=0.05, M2=0.03, alpha_deg=4.0)
    pp.zoo.evaluate("airfoil_cst_rans_mlp")             # recomputes the card's metrics on the stored reference
    pp.zoo.validate("airfoil_cst_rans_mlp").decisao     # TrustReport: APPROVED | REVIEW | REJECT
    print(pp.zoo.catalogue())                           # every model and dataset: metrics, size, Hub link
    print(pp.zoo.anchors.catalogue())                   # the same models as a named family, one per problem
    res = pp.zoo.finetune("airfoil_cst_rans_mlp", (X_new, Y_new), save_to="my_airfoil")  # refused if worse

Only models that passed the zoo's gate ship (see ``_catalog.py`` and ``docs/dev/model_dataset_inventory.md``).
Weights and datasets are listed in ``manifest.json`` with SHA-256 and versions; small files are bundled, the rest is
downloaded lazily from the Hugging Face Hub (``PINNeAPPle-Labs``). ``pp.datasets`` is :mod:`pinneapple_hub.zoo.datasets`.

classes.doc: The fine-tuned model is worse than the original on the original test set (pass ``force=True`` to save it).

methods.doc:
Save the fine-tuned model; refused (:class:`FinetuneRejectedError`) if it is worse than the original on
the original test set, unless ``force``.

functions.doc:
Export a model to ONNX (pre/post-processing included; parity with PyTorch checked to 1e-5). See
:func:`pinneapple_hub.zoo.export.export_onnx`.

functions.sig: (name: ModelRef, onnx_model, X = None, *, offline: bool | None = None) -> float
functions.doc: Largest scaled difference between an ONNX graph and the PyTorch model (:mod:`pinneapple_hub.zoo.export`).

functions.sig: (name: ModelRef, inputs = None, *, offline: bool | None = None, **named) -> builtins.list
functions.doc: Per-query trust checks and verdict for each input row (:mod:`pinneapple_hub.zoo.checks`).

functions.doc: Names of the shipped models (optionally only those whose task or tags mention ``task``).

functions.name: info
functions.sig: (name: str, *, offline: bool | None = None, version: str | None = None) -> ModelCard
functions.doc:
The model card (``ModelCard``): task, inputs/outputs with units, validity range, metrics against the
reference, training data, licence, citation and the stored trust report. ``print(card.to_markdown())``.

functions.name: load
functions.sig: (name: str, *, offline: bool | None = None, version: str | None = None) -> ZooModel
functions.doc:
A ready-to-use predictor (weights verified against the manifest's SHA-256). ``version`` loads a superseded
release (see :func:`versions`; a ``SupersededModelWarning`` says why it was superseded).

functions.name: versions
functions.doc: Every release of a model, newest first, with the reason each older one was superseded.

functions.name: predict
functions.doc: ``load(name).predict(...)`` in one call.

functions.name: catalogue
functions.doc:
Markdown page of every model and dataset: metrics, trust decision, size, Hugging Face link
(``docs/guides/zoo_catalogue.md`` is this page).

functions.name: status
functions.doc: Where each file of a model resolves from right now (bundled | cached | remote), without downloading.

functions.name: evaluate
functions.sig: (name: ModelRef, dataset = None, *, split: str | None = None, offline: bool | None = None, rtol: float | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]
functions.doc:
Metrics of a model against reference cases.

``dataset``: None (the model's own reference splits, e.g. held-out test + NACA reference for the airfoil),
a dataset name (with ``split``), a ``DatasetSplit``, an ``(inputs, outputs)`` pair or a mapping of columns.
With the stored reference, the result also says whether the card's metrics are reproduced (``matches_card``).

functions.name: validate
functions.sig: (name: ModelRef, inputs = None, *, offline: bool | None = None)
functions.doc:
Trust report (``pinneapple_analysis.trust.TrustReport``) of a model: its card metrics reproduced on the stored
reference, the acceptance limits of the zoo gate, the model's physics checks and -- if ``inputs`` are given --
whether they are inside the validity range (an out-of-range warning is raised for those that are not).

functions.name: finetune
functions.sig: (name: ModelRef, new_data, *, epochs: int = 200, lr: float = 0.0001, batch: int = 256, weight_decay: float = 0.0, tolerance: float = 0.02, seed: int = 0, force: bool = False, save_to: str | Path | None = None, registry: str | Any | None = None, replay: bool = True, new_test = None, offline: bool | None = None, progress = None) -> FinetuneResult
functions.doc:
Fine-tune a copy of a zoo model on ``new_data`` (``(inputs, outputs)``, a dataset split or a mapping of
columns; NaN outputs are ignored) and check it on the model's ORIGINAL held-out test set.

The fine-tuned model is ``accepted`` when none of its guard metrics (the card's primary held-out errors) got worse
than the original's by more than ``tolerance`` (relative). With ``save_to`` (a directory) or ``registry`` (an
``ArtifactRegistry``, a ``ModelStore`` or a registry root path), a rejected model raises
:class:`FinetuneRejectedError` and nothing is written, unless ``force=True``. ``new_test``: optional held-out
cases of the new data, reported in ``new_data_metrics``. ``replay`` (default True) mixes the model's original
training split into the fine-tuning set, the usual guard against forgetting what the model already knew.

functions.name: benchmark
functions.sig: (name: ModelRef, *, budget_s: float = 60.0, seeds: int = 1, baselines: Sequence[str] = ('retrain',), out_dir: str | Path = 'zoo_benchmark', force: bool = False, log = print, **kwargs)
functions.doc:
Benchmark a zoo model with ``pp.benchmark``: the shipped model against the same architecture retrained from
scratch on the same training split under ``budget_s`` seconds (CPU), on the same held-out test set, with
``pp.benchmark``'s gates, report and trust card. Returns its ``BenchmarkResult``. Needs
``pinneapple_analysis.benchmark``.
